title: Make a scored selection recomputable
statement: Choose topics or texts by an open score whose factors, weights and totals anyone can recompute, and let a person override it only with a recorded reason.
detail: In its queue of work after feedback on the reading course, the project made two things preserve-obligations: a topic scorecard whose every topic record exposes factor values, weights, total and verdict, so the verdict can be recomputed, and a visible human override where a person can keep or reject a topic against the score with a recorded reason (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/feedback-obligations.jsonl`). The curriculum packet requires a topic score replay showing factors, weights, formula result, human override and final verdict (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/curriculum-agent.md`).
against: The same obligations say the praise applied to the approach, not to the metric's calibration, and that a human override is a governance control, not evidence that the chosen topic is effective (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/feedback-obligations.jsonl`). It rests on one review's endorsement, not on a measured outcome. the same review could not yet follow one factor of the score, a load-bearing metric, and asked for it to be explained, so a formula is only open to challenge once its factors are (the same file).

evidence.quote: Every topic record exposes factor values, weights, total, and verdict.

Human override is a governance control, not evidence that the selected topic is effective.
Topic score replay showing factors, weights, formula result, human override, and final verdict.
praises the transparent scorecard, human override
transparent plan-first topic scoring, reasoned human override
They can challenge the weightings, inspect what falls out, and push on a decision they disagree with.
A person overrode the score and gave a reason rather than allowing the number to decide.

**Override** = a keep that contradicts the score, justified by a *limitation of the scorecard itself*.
